title: Halting after an amplified run
statement: Let $N$ be a finite-state nondeterministic Turing machine on Boolean inputs, let $r,T,m$ be natural numbers, and let $\mathrm{dec}:\mathbb{N}\to\{0,1\}$. Suppose every choice word of length $T$ makes $N$ halt on input $x$. For a run index $j\in\{0,\ldots,r\}$, counter $c\in\{0,\ldots,r+1\}$, and configuration $D$ of the amplified machine, suppose every work-tape block with index greater than $j$ is blank with its head at $0$. Also suppose that, from every configuration in the rewind phase for run $j$, every choice word of length $m$ makes the amplified machine halt. Then every choice word of length $T+m$, started from the embedding of $N$’s initial configuration at run $j$ and counter $c$ into $D$, makes the amplified machine halt.
